ranked_hypotheses.name: Pleistocene Lake Lahontan shoreline displacement as an independent paleogeodetic datum
ranked_hypotheses.expected_dti_improvement: Moderate conditional potential: a demonstrable offset of a laterally continuous, age-matched shoreline can be a direct displacement signal where modern scarps are subdued. Transfer is uncertain because shoreline deformation may be older than the competition target faults.
ranked_hypotheses.implementation_cost: High: obtain and pin high-resolution DEM tiles and mapped shoreline geometry; separate shoreline age/level, estimate local wave-cut surfaces, fit displacement/tilt across multiple segments, and preregister positive/negative controls before holdout evaluation.
layers: Official USGS 3DEP 1 m bare-earth DEM tiles (raw elevations; a 100 m derivative is not an adequate substitute).
Age/level-tagged Lake Lahontan shoreline or lacustrine-unit geometry from the USGS National Geologic Map Database (NGMDB), after checking the specific map scale and attributes.
Native Band 12 det_elev and Band 19 det_elev_slope for broad geomorphic context; optional Band 15 depth_to_base_surf and Band 13 iso_grav_anom as independent structural context.
ranked_hypotheses.targeted_physical_signature: Within a single mapped highstand shoreline level, estimate a locally detrended shoreline bench surface and detect a narrow, strike-coherent step or tilt that offsets the same-age bench across a corridor, repeats on adjacent shoreline segments, and is independently consistent with subsurface structure. The shoreline is a positive displacement marker, not a generic elevation contour or a fault label.
ranked_hypotheses.why_it_may_find_uncatalogued_faults: An unmapped fault can displace a formerly near-level lacustrine bench while leaving little fresh topographic scarp; age-matched geomorphic surfaces provide a differential reference even where the modern fault trace is obscured.
ranked_hypotheses.named_non_fault_mimic: Wave-cut bench relief and variable shoreline facies, local lake-level/age miscorrelation, differential compaction of lacustrine sediment, erosional terrace risers, and volcanic-flow margins. Require multiple same-level segments, map-scale uncertainty, and independent controls.
ranked_hypotheses.difference_from_repository_methods: Repository searches show Lahontan shorelines are usually treated as a mimic to suppress or mask. No exact operator was found that uses a mapped same-age shoreline as a positive displacement datum and tests repeated cross-bench throw. Existing scarp and knickpoint detectors search for local edges or channel anomalies rather than correlated displacement of a dated shoreline surface.

ranked_hypotheses.name: Time-ordered earthquake-sequence migration along blind fault planes
ranked_hypotheses.expected_dti_improvement: Low-to-moderate and highly uncertain: temporal migration could identify active concealed fault strands, but local event coverage, catalog completeness, and agreement between active sequences and the competition labels may be sparse.
ranked_hypotheses.implementation_cost: Very high relative to a native-only raster method: retrieve and quality-filter event origin time, depth, location uncertainty and magnitude; decluster or separate swarms from aftershocks; fit migration/plane hypotheses; then evaluate with spatially buffered folds and negative controls.
layers: USGS ComCat event catalog: origin time, hypocenter, magnitude, event type, and location uncertainty; do not infer timing from static native count bands.
Native Band 7 geod_shearrate and Band 8 geod_dilaterate only as independent spatial context after their physical identity and fold handling are checked.
Optional native Band 13 iso_grav_anom and Band 17 cond_surf as independent structural context, not labels.
ranked_hypotheses.targeted_physical_signature: Repeated, quality-filtered earthquake sequences whose hypocenters migrate coherently along a fitted buried plane or along-strike corridor through time, with sequence direction and depth evolution that persist under completeness thresholds and are not simply a static density hotspot.
ranked_hypotheses.why_it_may_find_uncatalogued_faults: A blind active fault can generate a migrating swarm or aftershock sequence before it expresses a mapped surface trace; ordered source motion can expose a connected structure that a coarse, static event-density raster smears out.
ranked_hypotheses.named_non_fault_mimic: Geothermal injection/production swarms, mining blasts, quarry sequences, volcanic or dike-intrusion swarms, aftershock migration on an already mapped fault, and apparent migration caused by changing network detection thresholds or hypocenter uncertainty.
ranked_hypotheses.difference_from_repository_methods: Executed repository features use static native earthquake-count/density fields and couple them to strain or conductivity. A spatial hypocenter-plane/RANSAC proposal also appears in an older review, so this proposal is deliberately narrower and different: no time-ordered event-migration operator or sequence-direction test was found in src/, scripts/, or hypothesis registries. It is not a claim that seismic clustering itself is new.

ranked_hypotheses.name: Age-tagged geologic-unit contact termination and offset graph
ranked_hypotheses.expected_dti_improvement: Low-to-moderate: potentially precise where several mapped contacts are exposed, but limited recall beneath continuous alluvium and vulnerable to geologic-map scale and compilation artifacts.
ranked_hypotheses.implementation_cost: High: acquire vector-unit polygons and metadata, harmonize scale/age attributes, remove fault annotations from predictors, construct contact correspondences with map uncertainty, and run explicit offset/shuffled-contact controls.
layers: USGS NGMDB or an explicitly identified state geological survey map product with attributed lithostratigraphic unit polygons and map-scale/age metadata.
Native Band 15 depth_to_base_surf, Band 2 rtp, Band 13 iso_grav_anom, and Band 17 cond_surf for independent evidence at candidate contact terminations.
Any fault-line attributes or catalogue-derived distance columns in the geology product are excluded from predictors.
ranked_hypotheses.targeted_physical_signature: A graph of age- and lithology-matched contact segments in which multiple independent bedrock contacts terminate, step, or show consistent lateral displacement across one candidate corridor, with a corresponding basement/potential-field break. Score displacement and correspondence, not the mere presence of a mapped contact or mapped fault line.
ranked_hypotheses.why_it_may_find_uncatalogued_faults: Fault displacement may juxtapose or truncate stratigraphic contacts in areas where no Quaternary fault line was digitized; matching several contacts can provide a structural continuation clue across gaps in the surface-fault inventory.
ranked_hypotheses.named_non_fault_mimic: Primary intrusive or volcanic contacts, depositional facies changes, alluvial cover boundaries, map-sheet joins, generalized contacts, age-correlation errors, and georeferencing mismatch.
ranked_hypotheses.difference_from_repository_methods: The available derived SGMC layer is a fault-proxy raster; the inspected lanes use potential-field edges and fault-line priors, not an age-aware graph that matches and tests offset lithologic polygon boundaries. No mapped-unit contact-displacement graph was found in the current source or hypothesis search.
